result:
The role comparison in the new filter code now goes through a helper in `@/lib/authorization`, not `user.role` directly. I did not run tests, lint, or the app, as you asked.

**What was wrong:** `src/features/users/utils/filter-users.ts` had `user.role === role` in the role filter.

**What I changed:**
- `src/lib/authorization.tsx`: added `hasRole(user, role)`, which returns `user.role === role`. The authorization module now holds the only role comparison in the new code.
- `src/features/users/utils/filter-users.ts`: imports `hasRole` from `@/lib/authorization` and uses `hasRole(user, role)` in place of the direct comparison.

The "All roles" option still short-circuits with `role === 'ALL'`, which compares the filter value, not a user's role.

`export-users-csv.ts` reads `user.role` only to write it into the CSV, not to make an access decision, so I left it alone.

I did not commit anything. Two things to check when you review: the helper takes `ROLES` and relies on TypeScript accepting the enum-to-literal comparison, which I expect but did not verify with `tsc`. Also, `hasRole` is a plain comparison, not a `POLICIES` entry, because it is a list filter rather than an ownership check.
